chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Abdul Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Beware of disputes/quarreling, for it inherits disgrace and manifests vulnerability.

key_terms.الْمَشَارَة: Quarreling, disputing, or engaging in contentious argument
key_terms.الْمُعْوِرَة: Vulnerability, weakness, or the state of being exposed/defeated

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social consequences of quarreling according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against *al-masharah* (quarreling), a term often interpreted by Shia scholars as either excessive argumentation or the act of showing off one's knowledge to gain prestige. He links this behavior to *al-ma'arrat* (lasting disgrace) and *al-mu'irah* (revealing inner weakness), emphasizing that such disputes erode spiritual dignity and expose the fragility of the ego. This hadith serves as a practical guide for maintaining humility and avoiding the social and spiritual consequences of contentiousness.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Beware of the disputes for it inherits the disgrace and manifests the vulnerability’.
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyabah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Guard (yourself) against engaging in disputes; it causes losses and reveals defects.”
